answer: Admission is not a fee but a drawn slot. Each round's signed round beacon seeds a lottery over registered names, and a name may vote only in the slots it drew. Holding k names forces a farm to seed k separate tickets whose winning frequency falls as the nebula of entrants thickens, and a beacon win cannot be transferred, traded, or backdated to another ticket. Unused slots simply expire, so stockpiling tickets buys no voyage advantage. Auditors read the beacon transcript per slot, where a cluster of names drawing identical sequences flags itself, and honest holders keep one ticket.
